top_categories.workout_context: Granfondo Bratislava's mixed terrain rewards steady threshold power. Surging and recovering costs more watts than just holding.
Race-pace efforts that mimic Granfondo Bratislava's demands. Pacing, fueling, and tactical decisions under fatigue. Practice the race before August.
At Granfondo Bratislava, surges push you above threshold and you have to recover while still riding. Over-unders train exactly that.
Granfondo Bratislava's mixed terrain forces constant power changes. Surge over the rough stuff, settle on the smooth, repeat for 82 miles.
88–92% FTP is where you'll spend the hardest sustained miles of Granfondo Bratislava. Train it until it feels boring.
When someone attacks on mixed terrain, you have 10 seconds to respond or you're off the back. This builds that response.
At mile 60 of 82, glycogen is gone. This workout teaches your body to produce watts on fumes.
Varied gradients on mixed terrain demand climbing versatility. Sit the shallow stuff, stand the steep stuff, switch without thinking.
Two threshold sessions per week without the recovery cost of VO2max work. For 82 miles, sustainable FTP gains matter more than peak power.
How long can you hold 105% FTP before you blow? At Granfondo Bratislava, that number decides whether you bridge or get dropped.
Every hard session works better with a bigger aerobic base. At 82 miles, base fitness is the difference between racing and surviving.
Endurance with intensity spikes baked in. Exactly what 3,600ft of climbing on mixed terrain does to your power file on race day.

race_overlay.nutrition: Target 60–80g carbs/hour for Granfondo Bratislava’s 82 miles. Start fueling within the first 30 minutes — early fueling prevents late-race collapse. Bonking at mile 60 is a nutrition failure, not a fitness failure.
race_overlay.terrain: Mixed terrain at Granfondo Bratislava requires surface adaptability. Include weekly rides on mixed terrain to build confidence.

pack_summary: This 10-workout pack focuses on TT Threshold, Race Simulation, and Over Under to prepare you for 82 miles of mixed terrain in Bratislava, Slovakia.
